title: One Special Needs Plans Enrollment in Force at a Time
content:
A member may hold only one Special Needs Plan at a time, and never alongside an ordinary Medicare Advantage plan, because Medicare allows one Medicare Advantage election in any coverage month. The greatest number of Special Needs Plans enrollments one member may hold at once is therefore 1.

## 1. The condition tested when a new election is recorded

> No other Special Needs Plan enrollment for the same member is in a status of enrollment submitted, eligibility verification, active or deemed continued eligibility on the day the new election is recorded.

The condition is tested on the enrollment register before the new election is recorded, and on what that register holds rather than on the member's own account of the plans they have. Enrollments are matched to the member the election is for. Each enrollment stands as a record of its own and is told apart from another by its contract year and its coverage effective date.

## 2. Where such an enrollment already stands

Where such an enrollment exists the new election is recorded as a plan change, and the earlier enrollment ends the day before the new coverage begins.

Enrollments in different contract years that do not overlap are not duplicates.

## 3. Where a member qualifies for two packages

A member who qualifies for two different Special Needs Plans is told what each would give them before either election is recorded, rather than being signed into whichever was mentioned first.

## 4. Points of judgement

| What the enrollment register holds for that member | Is the condition met? |
| --- | --- |
| No other Special Needs Plans enrollment at all | Met |
| Another enrollment standing at enrollment submitted | Not met |
| Another enrollment at eligibility verification | Not met |
| Another active enrollment | Not met |
| Another enrollment in deemed continued eligibility | Not met |
| Another enrollment already disenrolled | Met |
| Another enrollment already terminated for loss of the qualifying need | Met |

The four statuses named in the condition are the whole of what bars a second election; an enrollment standing in any other status does not bar it. A second enrollment in a contract year that does not overlap the first is likewise not a duplicate.
